name: progress-bar
description: Live progress bars in the status line and a docked Status panel for subagents and long jobs that write ~/.claude-progress/<slug>.json

statusLine.title: Progress status line
statusLine.description: Show the progress bars in the status line with no setup. A status line you already had still prints below them.

openPanel.title: Open the Status panel
openPanel.description: Open the Status panel beside the chat at session start, until /progress-bar panel off.

autoReport.title: Report work automatically
autoReport.description: Claude shows multi-step work as progress bars without being asked, and a long busy turn shows as a working row until it ends. Off, rows come only from task lists, long commands, subagents and progress_report calls.

usageMeter.title: Usage meter
usageMeter.description: Show your plan usage (7-day percent) in the Status panel. To read it, one session per machine runs a tiny Claude Haiku call (claude -p) every 30 minutes on your login, which counts toward your usage.

hideEmails.title: Hide account emails
hideEmails.description: Mask account emails in the status line, the Status panel and the Chrome line, for screen sharing.

inlineSteps.title: Inline step checklist
inlineSteps.description: Show a running job's step checklist under its row in the Status panel, without opening its card. Off, the checklist shows only in the opened card.

groupChat.title: Group chat
groupChat.description: Off by default. On, this session gets chat_read and chat_say for the machine's group chat (needs the agent daemon, docs/agent-daemon.md). The collaborator's new chat lines are attached to your own next prompt as quoted data, marked as untrusted messages, not instructions, and capped. A toast says when lines were attached. Your permission prompts still apply.

agentLink.title: Agent link
agentLink.description: Off by default. On, the plugin sets up the agent daemon (bin/agentd.py) once a secure channel exists: it installs and starts a background service (a LaunchAgent on macOS, a systemd user service on Linux) so your agents and a collaborator's agents can message each other. Off, the plugin never installs or starts a service.
